takeaways: A guide to March 2026 in the Twin Cities. On St. Patrick's Day you can catch two parades: Saint Paul's (Minnesota's largest) at noon from Rice Park to Mears Park, followed by a party at CHS Field, then Minneapolis's 6:30 p.m. parade on Nicollet Mall.

Sports: Timberwolves games at Target Center all month and nine Wild home games at Grand Casino Arena, with afternoon start times on some weekends. West Seventh and Cathedral Hill get busy on game nights.
The Minneapolis Home + Garden Show (February 25 to March 1) draws more than 55,000 people, with a plant sale after 5 p.m. on the last day. The Twin Cities Home Expo follows April 24 to 26.

Theater: Macbeth, Sleuth and The Mousetrap at the Guthrie; Water for Elephants at the Orpheum; Kimberly Akimbo and Mrs. Doubtfire at the Ordway; plus shows at the Children's Theatre, the Fitzgerald and First Avenue.

Development: the Heights in Saint Paul (a 112-acre, roughly $430 million redevelopment) is finishing its public infrastructure, and MSP Airport has about half a billion dollars of 2026 projects, including Concourse G and Terminal 2 expansions.

Market snapshot at the time: Minneapolis median in the mid-$300,000s with about 42 days on market (up from 37) and about $217 per square foot; Saint Paul around $295,000 with about 31 days on market and about $189 per square foot. March is the time to prepare for the spring market.

faq.q: Are there two St. Patrick's Day parades in the Twin Cities?
faq.a: Yes. Saint Paul's parade, Minnesota's largest, runs at noon downtown, and Minneapolis holds its own evening parade on Nicollet Mall, so you can attend both on the same day.

faq.q: When does the spring real estate market start in the Twin Cities?
faq.a: Activity typically picks up in April, so March is the time to get pre-approved, hire an agent and finish pre-sale improvements, according to the video.

takeaways: A tour of a Country Joe model in The Preserve in Lakeville, a development where Country Joe Homes is the exclusive builder and homes range from about $800,000 to $1.5 million. Phase 1 had sold out, with lots left in Phases 2 and 3 at the time.
The Preserve is about 20 minutes from the airport and downtown Minneapolis, about 15 minutes from the Mall of America, with walking and bike trails in the neighborhood.

About 4,800 square feet with six bedrooms and five baths, priced around $1,115,000 at the time. The main floor has 9-foot ceilings, a large island with a five-burner range, a butler's pantry with a dishwasher and sink, a mudroom, and a main-floor bedroom with a three-quarter bath.

Upstairs are a loft, laundry, an owner's suite with a soaking tub, a bedroom with its own bath and two bedrooms sharing a Jack-and-Jill bath. The lower level adds a large family room, another bedroom, a bath and storage, with zoned heating.
Country Joe Homes is based in Lakeville and has built there for decades. Jason notes Airlake Industrial Park helps keep Lakeville's property taxes lower.

faq.q: What is The Preserve in Lakeville?
faq.a: A Country Joe Homes community in Lakeville with homes from about $800,000 to $1.5 million, plus neighborhood walking and bike trails.

takeaways: A January tour of a modern home on acreage in Prior Lake, in a secluded neighborhood between Shakopee and Prior Lake: about 4,700 square feet with five bedrooms, five baths and a four-car garage, priced at $1,179,000 at the time.

The main floor has 10-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling windows of about 7 feet, a rectangular fireplace, a kitchen with roughly 60-inch upper cabinets, built-in knife slots, an island seating four and a hidden pantry behind the range wall, plus a large office and a mudroom.
Upstairs are three bedrooms, each with a bath (one shared), laundry, and an owner's suite with a vaulted ceiling, soaking tub, separate water closet and hilltop views.

The lower level adds a family room with a wet bar, a fifth bedroom, a full bath and storage. The insulated, finished four-car garage is plumbed for gas, and the hilltop lot has boulder retaining walls.

faq.q: What does about $1.2 million buy in Prior Lake?
faq.a: In this tour, a modern 4,700-square-foot home with five bedrooms, five baths and a four-car garage on a secluded hilltop lot.

takeaways: Five overlooked suburbs, with prices as stated in the video. West St. Paul: just south of Saint Paul, homes in the mid-$300,000s to low $400,000s, the 460-acre Dodge Nature Center (free), 16 city parks, an ice arena and a pool, with errands along South Robert Street.

Savage: 15 to 20 miles southwest of downtown, homes in the low to mid-$400,000s, 23 parks, about 30 miles of paved trails and 60 miles of sidewalks connected to Murphy-Hanrehan Park Reserve, plus Dakota Landing Park and a downtown with good restaurants.

Richfield: about 7 square miles, surrounded by Minneapolis and Bloomington, about 7 miles from downtown and 5 minutes from the Mall of America. Homes in the mid-$300,000s (up about 3.6% over a year), 23 parks and Wood Lake Nature Center (about 150 acres). Best Buy is headquartered here.

Mendota Heights: where the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers meet, near Fort Snelling, with Oheyawahi (Pilot Knob), a sacred Dakota site with bluff-top views. Homes run from the high $500,000s to mid-$600,000s and up.

Golden Valley: about 5 miles from downtown Minneapolis, next to the 750-plus-acre Theodore Wirth Park, with Brookview Park and its golf course. Homes, from ramblers to mid-century moderns, were in the mid-$400,000s.

faq.q: What are affordable first-ring suburbs near Minneapolis and Saint Paul?
faq.a: Jason points to West St. Paul and Richfield, with homes in the mid-$300,000s at the time of the video, plus Golden Valley in the mid-$400,000s.

faq.q: Where do the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers meet?
faq.a: At Mendota Heights, near Fort Snelling. Oheyawahi (Pilot Knob), a sacred Dakota site, overlooks the confluence.

takeaways: A January tour of a Key Land Homes model at Sapphire Lake in Farmington, one of the farthest southeast suburbs: under 30 minutes to the airport and under 40 minutes to either downtown, near Highway 52 and about 10 minutes from I-35W.
Four bedrooms, three baths, about 2,100 finished square feet and a four-car garage, priced around $590,000 at the time.

The standout is a great room with ceilings of about 12 to 14 feet and huge windows, plus a kitchen with a five-burner gas cooktop and seating for about five at the island. The home backs up to a walking trail and protected wetland.
Upstairs are four bedrooms, laundry and an owner's suite. The unfinished lookout basement is plumbed for a bath; Jason estimates finishing it at about $45,000 to $60,000.

faq.q: How much does it cost to finish a basement in a new home?
faq.a: Jason estimates about $45,000 to $60,000 to finish a lower level like the one in this Farmington home, with a bedroom, bath and family room.

takeaways: Jason's spring market forecast: with about 7,700 homes for sale and about 50 days on market, the Twin Cities are still technically a seller's market, but leverage depends on the home. The median was in the mid-$300,000s to low $390,000s, up about 3%.

Spring demand lands first on well-located, updated homes, like those near the Chain of Lakes or in Edina and Minnetonka. A move-in-ready home near Lake Harriet can get multiple offers in days while a dated home three miles away sits for 60.

What stalls in spring: overpricing based on last year's sales, deferred maintenance (buyers mentally add $30,000 to $50,000 for dated kitchens and baths) and sellers waiting for spring to fix their problems.

Timing: late February to early March gives sellers of average homes less competition; late March through April brings a listing surge where pricing mistakes get punished; May and June are peak competition for the best homes, which historically sell at 100% or more of list price.

Buyers: get pre-approved now, act early to avoid bidding wars, and stay flexible, for example St. Louis Park instead of Edina (the Green Line Extension opens in 2027), or an updated older home in Northeast instead of new construction.
Sellers: prep in January and February, price right from day one and watch days on market in your area.

faq.q: When is the best time to list a house in the Twin Cities?
faq.a: It depends on the home. Average homes often do best listed in late February or early March, before the April surge of listings. Top-tier, move-in-ready homes can benefit from peak demand in late March through June.

faq.q: Is spring a good time to buy a home in Minneapolis?
faq.a: Early spring is. Buyers have more negotiating room in February and March; by May and June, the best homes see multiple offers and less room for inspection contingencies.
